title: fix(core): the batch-equivalence recorder snapshots `where`, so the golden records the query as issued
body:
Fixes #19141

Clause-②: no

## The defect was in the EVIDENCE, not in the behaviour

`resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json` is the committed record of **which
queries the authz resolver issues**. One of its 11 recorded `sys_position` reads was not the
query that was issued.

The recording double stored `opts.where` **by reference**. `sys_position` is read as
`{ name: { $in: grants.positions } }` — the `$in` **is** the live `grants.positions` array —
and step 6c then runs `grants.positions.unshift(BUILTIN_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_ADMIN)` on that same
array, after the read has already gone out. Step 6a also *reassigns* `grants.positions` to a
filtered copy when a position is deactivated, so the stored reference could diverge in either
direction depending on fixture data.

The resolver's behaviour is correct and unchanged — the `unshift` is deliberate. What was wrong
is what the recorder captured. A pin that misdescribes its subject is worse than a missing pin:
it read green while certifying a read no driver ever saw, in the one file nobody re-derives
because it is supposed to be the derivation.

## What changed (3 files, all test-layer)

1. `packages/core/src/security/__tests__/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.testkit.ts` —
   the recorder now takes a deep **snapshot** of `where` at record time. `structuredClone` is
   called without a `?? null` normalisation, so an absent `where` still records as absent
   rather than as a value no caller ever passed.
2. `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json` — the one
   corrupted entry corrected. A **one-line** diff.
3. `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.test.ts` — two
   failure-capable pins.

## The golden was corrected by re-capture from its own declared source

⛔ Not re-captured to agree with new output. The golden's header names its source as the
pre-batch **sequential** implementation, `git show 795ea05a7:packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`.
That file was materialised and driven against these exact fixtures with the fixed recorder, as
a one-time probe (deleted before commit).

The sequential implementation issues, for `permission-set-derived-grants`:

```
{"object":"sys_position","where":{"name":{"$in":["org_member","everyone"]}},"limit":200,"isSystem":true}
```

⇒ `platform_admin` was **not** in the array when the query went out. The corrected golden
records that, and it is byte-equal to what today's batched implementation issues — which is the
equivalence property this suite exists to prove, now resting on a faithful instrument.

### The card's declared evidence limit is now closed

The filing card left it "⛔ not established" whether any *other* recorded leg in this golden is
also post-mutation. A **full** re-capture diffed every recorded leg of all 11 fixtures against
the committed golden. Exactly one divergence, the one above. Every other leg was already
faithful.

## The pins can fail — measured, not asserted

Ablation, run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` so the mutation is proven on disk (anchor
1 to 0, blob `caaf4f8c2d3c` to `7c76f56159d7`) and proven restored afterwards (`blob == HEAD`,
`git diff HEAD` empty). Restoring `where: opts?.where` turns **3** tests red:

- `a where array the caller mutates after the read keeps its issue-time contents`
- `records the real sys_position read without the platform_admin unshifted in afterwards`
- `permission-set-derived-grants > issues the SAME reads ...`

The third is the corrected golden's own assertion, so golden and recorder now hold each other
honest. Neither new pin is satisfiable by re-capturing from a by-reference recorder: they assert
against the read **as issued**.

⚠️ Recorded because it matters: the **first** ablation attempt was a no-op. A trap in the same
shell restored the file before the test ran, and the run came back green — reading exactly like
"the mutation landed and the pins held". That reading was voided and the ablation redone as a
single-shot. It is the false green the ablation tooling exists to stop.

## Verification

All on final head `b4a47e9dd`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core build && test && typecheck` — 51 files, **1321 tests**, all pass.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` — **51 derived, 51 run,
  0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, every family carrying a recorded exit code, none of them 3.
  Three gates first exited **3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET)** for want of a built workspace; the
  workspace was built (72/72 tasks) and all three re-ran green.
- 3 extra artifact-roster gates run beyond the derived union, because the derivation flagged
  their rosters as sitting under a directory one of my paths is in, where silence is evidence
  in neither direction: `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`,
  `check:filter-alias-parity` — all exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`) — exit 0. The full union, so no
  narrowing claim is being made.
- `origin/main` merged in; the 4 commits it brought touch **zero** files under `packages/`, so
  there is no overlap with this diff.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset` is warranted, and it was **measured**, not assumed. `@objectstack/core` ships
`["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`. Against the built `dist`:

| symbol | files in `packages/core/dist` |
|---|--:|
| `makeRecordingQl` | 0 |
| `batch-equivalence` | 0 |
| `structuredClone(opts` | 0 |
| `permission-set-derived-grants` | 0 |
| `resolveUserAuthzGrants` (positive control) | 4 |
| `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_PLATFORM_ADMIN` (positive control) | 4 |

⇒ instrument lit in both directions; this diff publishes nothing. **The label itself was not
written** — this dispatch's write budget is two REST calls (the report comment and this PR) and
does not include a label write, so applying `skip-changeset` is left to the seat.

## Acceptance notes

Observations, noted and deliberately **not** filed — neither is a reproducible defect, a
declared-contract violation, or a metadata-authoring trap:

- The `where` snapshot is the only reference the recorder held; `object`, `limit` and `isSystem`
  are immutable scalars. Carrier: this PR, already handled here.
- The production `unshift` at step 6c does mutate an array the resolver has already handed to a
  query. It is correct today only because the query is `await`ed to completion first. This is a
  real latent hazard, but it is behaviour, not evidence, and the card explicitly fences it out
  ("⛔ Not a claim that the resolver's behaviour is wrong"). Upcoming carrier: none — the dispatch's own
  enumeration of the 33 open PRs found none touching `resolve-authz-context.ts`. Flagged here rather
  than filed because filing it would re-open a question the card already ruled on.
